newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X says talks on Busang going slowly.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X says talks on Busang going slowly.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp are still working on forging a joint venture to mine the huge Busang gold find in Indonesia, but talks are moving slowly, Bre-X chief executive David Walsh said on Thursday.
"We're moving ahead, albeit at a snail's pace," Walsh told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"We're trying to get them to appreciate our views and the legal stance that we've taken," he said. Walsh made it clear he still had high hopes that Indonesian President Suharto would allow an auction for Bre-X's stake in Busang.
"We're not saying anything until we talk directly to the government of Indonesia," Borg said.

The Indonesian government has asked Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick to develop the world-class gold deposit on the island of Borneo, with Barrick getting 75 percent of the joint venture and Bre-X keeping 25 percent.

Negotiations between the two companies were clouded on Wednesday when senior mining officials told Reuters in Jakarta that Bre-X's application for crucial contracts of work for Busang had been canceled. Umar Said, secretary general of the Mines Ministry, said Bre-X and Barrick should apply together.
"They must set up a joint venture company and make a fresh application for contracts of work," he told Reuters on Thursday.
However, Bre-X's Walsh said two of his company officials had met with Umar on Thursday and heard a different message.
"The telephone call that I got from Rolie (Francisco), he was quite pleased with the meeting," Walsh said. "He said we're making very good progress in our relationship (with the Mines Ministry)."
Walsh said Bre-X was told its permits and applications were in good standing.

Walsh said Umar had apologized for the misunderstanding. Walsh reiterated a Bre-X statement released earlier today which said Umar's comments were "erroneously reported in a December 11 Reuters newswire article."
Peter Thomas, the Reuters company spokesman in London, said Reuters was confident the quotations in its December 11 story from Jakarta were accurate.
Walsh said he is waiting for word from the Indonesian president about opening up a bidding process for Busang. But, he said, Bre-X had not made a formal request.
"We understand that the (Indonesian) president is reviewing the situation," he said.
Placer Dome has formally asked for an open bidding process but had still received no response.
Placer Dome said on Thursday it was confused by the latest developments about Bre-X's status.
"We really don't know what is going to come from this," said spokesman Hugh Leggatt. But he said suggestions that an auction for the deposit may be launched were encouraging.
"Any indication of an open bidding process is positive for us and quite heartening," he said.
